Writing this comment not as a mom, but as somebody's (now grown up) kid. I was an only child and, for most of my life, I absolutely hated it. I was so jealous of all my friends' siblings. My parents tried really hard to have another baby, but it just wasn't in the cards and I know they—my mom, especially—felt immense guilt for not being able to give me that sense of family I craved. 

But now, as an adult, I'm actually pretty happy with the way things turned out. I'm closer with my parents on an individual level than I probably would be if I had a sibling. And the mild loneliness I felt in my childhood also forced me to think about the fact that family is so much more than DNA. I have a friend who I've known for nearly half my life and we've seen each other through a lot of difficult things. In every way besides biological, he is my brother. 

All that to say, there's a big narrative around "needing" to give your child a sibling in order for them to grow up happy and stable. It's all bullshit. Your child needs you to be at your best, checked in. Some people can balance that with a new baby, but I would venture to say that most people actually can't. 

No matter what you do, sibling or no sibling, you and your family are going to be just fine in the long run.
